listing.name: Castlevania: Symphony of the Night — PS1 / SymphonyRecomp
listing.summary: Register an already permitted working SymphonyRecomp v0.5.1b Windows player with your own US disc, preserving its existing .NET host, actual profile, cards, mods and upstream updater.

steps.title: Use an already permitted working official copy
steps.instruction: Use an already permitted official v0.5.1b Windows x64 sotn.exe copy in the scope of the publisher’s explicit released-player invitation and own-original instructions. That narrower context is not a top-level/mod source or redistribution license; RecompOne MIT does not license the whole project/mod package. Keep actual selected-copy use conditions and all applicable notices. This route does not clear the broader existing distribution/source-grant conditions.

steps.title: Keep the existing runtime and native entry
steps.instruction: Retain the complete working copy, adjacent DLL/native dependencies and its functioning player-owned .NET10 runtime context. Select sotn.exe, not sotn.dll, system dotnet.exe, a generator or updater staging helper. This release is framework-dependent; Portcove does not install/configure a nested .NET runtime or synthesize DOTNET_ROOT. Finish normal upstream setup outside Core before registration.

steps.title: Bind the actual profile and owned original
steps.instruction: Use your own North-American Symphony of the Night SLUS-00067/SLUS_000.67 CHD or CUE with all referenced data/audio BIN tracks. Preserve the complete original set/path for streaming; do not substitute known Japanese/European or Nocturne/XBLA inputs. Select the actual established writable runtime/profile working directory, normally the extracted root, and one literal argument token containing the absolute CHD/CUE path. Preserve spaces inside that token and the creating custom CWD. No --rom/--config/--no-updater or profile environment switch is established.

steps.title: Review intent and choose Play separately
steps.instruction: Review and consent to the exact executable, working directory and one original-path argument; registration does not prepare or start the game. Choose Play separately. Ordinary runtime is in the same apphost; upstream self-update stages/replaces/relaunches through successors outside Core’s selected-process observation. Its bounded wait is not proof the original exited or that successor arguments/custom profile are preserved. Let upstream finish and close all actual players before manual changes/relink. Upstream/player retains runtime replacement; Core does not compete with it.

steps.title: Preserve the whole creating profile and custom cards
steps.instruction: Keep the full runtime, original and actual CWD-relative settings.json/interface.ini, carda.sav/cardb.sav, all .sav/backup/config files, disc and mods including shipped executable sources/.cache and player edits, diagnostics and all unknown/custom outputs. Preserve absolute CardAPath/CardBPath targets separately; relative cards follow actual CWD. Preserve any upstream-owned external updater/recovery evidence. No new managed mod merge, backup, state migration or cross-build compatibility is granted. Removing registration removes only Core metadata and preserves external bytes.

warnings: The inspected upstream boot-identity checks are not full-disc cryptographic authentication. Earlier actual v0.5.1b Windows CHD/window/normal-close observations keep their exact scope; this batch adds no game execution or gameplay/save/load qualification and inherits nothing from another Castlevania port.

The selected tag uses AutoUpdateEnabled in interface.ini; current-source updater options differ. No CLI/environment disable is established, and non-owning registration need not disable the upstream updater. Managed host provisioning, pre-check updater control, mod ownership/merge and actual lifecycle qualification remain unresolved stronger work.

No Core-managed acquisition/setup/Install/Update/Backup/Rollback/migration/external deletion, package/build/source authenticity, exclusive successor-session or sandbox guarantee is offered. Project/mod source and redistribution applicability remain distinct from an already permitted player copy; selection itself grants no rights or Supported/native/installed/protected acceptance.
